source: Deletang et al. (2024) Language Modeling Is Compression (ICLR)
finding: A text-trained LLM used with arithmetic coding is a lossless compressor that beats domain tools on images and audio. Prediction and compression are the same thing.
numbers: Chinchilla 70B: ImageNet patches 43.4% of raw size (PNG 58.5%); LibriSpeech 16.4% (FLAC 30.3%). Offline setting, 1GB datasets.
quote: Chinchilla 70B ... compresses ImageNet patches to 43.4% and LibriSpeech samples to 16.4% of their raw size
limits: Raw rate ignores model size. Once parameter size is counted (adjusted rate), scaling past a point worsens compression; optimal model size depends on dataset size.
agent_relevance: Supports reading model fit as code length (S7). Gives no help on choosing among candidate rules inside one task.

source: Deletang et al. (2024) Language Modeling Is Compression, scaling section
finding: The compression view adds a model-size penalty to scaling laws: a bigger model must pay for its own weights. Small Transformers trained on enwik overfit to text and fail on other modalities.
numbers: Small Transformers (200K to 3.2M) trained on enwik8 compress ImageNet only to about 62% of raw size, near gzip (70.7%).
limits: Table was garbled in text extraction; only the abstract figures are fully safe to cite.
agent_relevance: A reminder that description length must include the cost of the rule itself, not only the fit (two-part code).

source: Huang et al. (2024) Compression Represents Intelligence Linearly (COLM)
finding: Across 31 public LLMs, average score on 12 benchmarks is almost linear in how well the model compresses fresh text.
numbers: Pearson about -0.95 in each of three domains (knowledge and commonsense, coding, math); 31 LLMs, 12 benchmarks.
limits: Base models only (fine-tuned models are not general compressors). Some models are outliers that likely overfit benchmarks. Accuracies above 0.8 hint at saturation. Correlation, not cause.
agent_relevance: Compression of held-out text is a contamination-resistant proxy for model strength; useful when picking which model fills a slot, not for per-problem decisions.

source: Huang et al. (2024) Compression Represents Intelligence Linearly, caveats
finding: The authors say the link may not hold for poorly trained models, and that the compression corpus size saturates.
numbers: Corpus size reaches saturation at around 3M (as stated in the paper); outlier models sit above the linear fit.
limits: Authors list limitations: only base models; findings may not hold for poorly trained LMs.
agent_relevance: Do not read a short code length alone as proof of capability; pair with held-out checks (G3).

source: Yoran et al. (2025) The Kolmogorov Test: Compression by Code Generation (ICLR)
finding: Ask a code LLM for the shortest program that prints a given byte sequence. Flagship models fail often.
numbers: Programs fail to reproduce the sequence 78% of the time (Llama-3.1-405B) and 40% (GPT-4o) on natural data; 66% and 45% on synthetic compositional data. Sequences of length 128.
limits: Metric cannot be gamed by wrong programs because a program must reproduce the data exactly. Prompted models' programs are larger than gzip on average (Precision above 1).
agent_relevance: Direct measurement that LLMs are weak at shortest-program search even on tiny data; so S7 must not trust a model's claim of 'simplest rule'. Code should count length and check exact reproduction.

source: Yoran et al. (2025) Kolmogorov Test, length and repetition findings
finding: Longer sequences are harder for prompted models. Most correct programs on real data just repeat the input, so they do not compress.
numbers: Audio-8-bit, Llama-405B accuracy: 47.1% at length 32, 29.9% at 64, 20.9% at 128, 14.2% at the next length (as read from Table 2); gzip compression rate improves 0.966 to 0.622 over the same range. Repetition accounts for over 95% of correct programs on natural data, 20% on synthetic.
limits: 2,000 audio sequences; 25 programs per modality hand-checked.
agent_relevance: A correct program is not a short program. Code should compute program length and reject a literal copy of the data as an explanation.

source: Yoran et al. (2025) Kolmogorov Test, trained models and scaffolds
finding: A 1.5B model trained on synthetic data beats prompted frontier models on synthetic data by over 40 points but not on real data. Chain of thought and execution feedback help little.
numbers: CoT on Llama: accuracy change of -1.3 (8B), -5.1 (70B), +2.1 (405B) points on average across modalities. Models trained on synthetic data reach near-zero on natural sequences.
limits: Execution feedback does not close the synthetic-to-real gap.
agent_relevance: Scaffolds that only add reasoning text barely help shortest-program search; search plus exact execution is what counts.

source: Grau-Moya et al. (2024) Learning Universal Predictors
finding: Train Transformers and LSTMs on data from random programs run on a universal Turing machine (BrainF-like) to approximate Solomonoff induction. They learn useful universal-style prediction and transfer to other tasks.
numbers: Tested on variable-order Markov sources (vs Bayes-optimal CTW) and 15 Chomsky-hierarchy tasks (6k sequences, 400 per task); Transformer-L best on Chomsky tasks by a margin.
limits: Transformers fail length generalisation; LSTMs generalise to longer sequences best. Small UTM and short sequences only.
agent_relevance: Shows a simplicity prior can be amortised into a network, but not into a prompt. For a frozen LLM it is a design hint only.

source: Ellis et al. (2021) DreamCoder: wake-sleep Bayesian program learning (PLDI)
finding: System that grows a program library by compressing solved programs (MDL/Bayes objective) and trains a neural guide on replayed and imagined tasks.
numbers: List-processing: before learning 3.7% solved in 10 min, after 79.6%; best SyGuS solver CVC4 82.4%; DreamCoder 84.3% with larger budget. LOGO and tower building: nearly 100% held-out vs no baseline above 60%. After 8 wake-sleep cycles 93% of physics laws and identities learned.
limits: Takes about a day on 20-100 CPUs per domain. Hand-built starting primitives.
agent_relevance: Library compression is the oldest working MDL loop for programs; the analog for our agent is saving reusable operator snippets.

source: Ellis et al. (2021) DreamCoder, memorise vs compress control
finding: Ablation: variants that store solved programs wholesale without compressing solved fewer held-out tasks than full DreamCoder in every domain.
numbers: Mean solve time 54.1s, median 15.0s for DreamCoder; baseline enumeration up to 400 million programs per task over 24 hours.
limits: Eight domains; per-domain figures not all read.
agent_relevance: Evidence that abstraction (shorter code through reuse), not recall, drives transfer.

source: Wang et al. (2024) Hypothesis Search: Inductive Reasoning with Language Models (ICLR)
finding: GPT-4 proposes natural-language hypotheses, turns each into Python, and keeps programs that pass all examples. Beats direct prompting on ARC.
numbers: 100 random ARC tasks: direct 17%, program only 23%, summarised hypotheses 30%, human-selected hypotheses 33%, human-written hypotheses 45%. 64 programs per task, 3 rounds of execution feedback.
limits: Small 100-task subset; GPT-4 only. Summaries are LLM-made.
agent_relevance: Closest published form of S2 plus S7: propose abstract rules, implement, execute on examples. The gain from a human filter (30 to 33) shows model ranking of hypotheses is weak.

source: Wang et al. (2024) Hypothesis Search, held-out behaviour
finding: When a generated program passes all training examples it almost always passes the test input.
numbers: Exactly one task was an exception, per the authors.
limits: ARC subset only. Our own data had two ARC programs that fit all examples and were wrong, so the pass-all filter is strong but not perfect.
agent_relevance: Keep pass-all-examples as a filter but add a held-out or mutated check (G3).

source: Grand et al. (2024) LILO: Learning Interpretable Libraries by Compressing and Documenting Code (ICLR)
finding: LLM writes programs, Stitch compresses them into abstractions by minimal description length, LLM names and documents each abstraction. Beats DreamCoder.
numbers: Test-split solve rate vs DreamCoder: +33.14 REGEX, +2.26 CLEVR, +20.42 LOGO. LLM solver alone vs DreamCoder: +32.20 REGEX, -5.83 CLEVR, +3.60 LOGO. One round of LLM synthesis costs about the same as 48 CPU-hours of DreamCoder search.
limits: Needs language annotations of tasks. Three domains only.
agent_relevance: Direct template for an LLM agent loop: synthesise, compress, document, reuse.

source: Grand et al. (2024) LILO, AutoDoc ablation
finding: Giving the LLM compressed but unnamed abstractions hurt. Adding auto-written names and docstrings fixed much of the loss.
numbers: Stitch compression without docs vs LLM solver: -30.60 REGEX, -2.91 CLEVR, -11.11 LOGO. AutoDoc then adds +9.73 REGEX, +2.27 CLEVR, +0.00 LOGO.
limits: On LOGO the docs did not help; authors blame semantic errors.
agent_relevance: Compression that makes text shorter but less readable harms an LLM reader. Score length and usability separately.

source: Ellis (2023) Human-like Few-Shot Learning via Bayesian Reasoning over Natural Language (NeurIPS)
finding: An LLM proposes natural-language hypotheses; a prior and likelihood reweigh them. With a prior tuned on human data it fits human number-game judgments.
numbers: R2 = .81 with held-out human responses, 50-100 proposals per problem. Switching from English hypotheses to Python significantly lowered fit. Human data: 8 participants in the number game.
limits: Fit is to the average of a few people. GPT-4's own judgments were decidedly different from humans.
agent_relevance: Natural-language rules as the hypothesis space can match human concepts better than code. A learned prior replaces raw length as the tie-break.

source: Li et al. (2025) Combining Induction and Transduction for Abstract Reasoning (ICLR)
finding: Same architecture and training data, trained to write programs (induction) or to predict outputs (transduction), solve different ARC tasks. Together they come close to average human level.
numbers: Best transduction with test-time training and no reranking: 56.75% on ARC validation. Induction and transduction results correlate with their own class across seeds, not the other class (p<.004). Comparison table lists the Akyurek ensemble at 61.9%.
limits: Models trained on synthetic LLM-written tasks. Ensemble rule: induction first, transduction as fallback.
agent_relevance: Program-like models are better at exact and compositional rules, direct prediction at fuzzy perception. Try the code route first, fall back otherwise.

source: Akyurek et al. (2025) The Surprising Effectiveness of Test-Time Training for Few-Shot Learning
finding: Brief weight updates on the task's own examples greatly lift an 8B model on ARC; ensembled with program synthesis it reaches 61.9%.
numbers: ARC public validation: 47.1% own fine-tuned model, 53.0% on BARC model, 61.9% ensembled with program synthesis. 80-task subset: fine-tuned 17.5% to 45.0% with TTT. BIG-Bench Hard 10-shot: 50.5% to 57.8%.
limits: Needs weight updates, so not a prompt-only scaffold. Pass@2.
agent_relevance: Shows a ceiling for scaffolds that cannot train; our agent must rely on program search plus checks.

source: Qiu et al. (2024) Phenomenal Yet Puzzling: Inductive Reasoning with Hypothesis Refinement (ICLR)
finding: LMs propose good rules but fail to apply them. With a symbolic interpreter filtering rules, results are strong; with an LM as interpreter they collapse.
numbers: Task accuracy falls from over 80% to almost zero on MiniSCAN when an LM applies the rule instead of an interpreter. Human reference: ConceptARC humans 90.9%.
limits: Several discrepancies from humans, including different sensitivity to noisy examples (12.5%, 25%, 50% perturbed).
agent_relevance: Rule induction by model, rule execution by code: the schema's split. Never let the model run its own rule.

source: Elmoznino et al. (2025) In-Context Learning and Occam's Razor (ICML)
finding: Next-token loss on in-context examples equals prequential code length, so ICL training jointly pushes for fit and simplicity of the implied model.
numbers: Train-risk ICL overfits; prequential ICL infers simpler functions closer to the truth (regression tasks, Mastermind); gains largest in low-data regimes.
limits: Current ICL underfits in large-data regimes on hard tasks; degree depends on architecture.
agent_relevance: Gives theory for why showing examples then asking for the rule can approximate MDL; not guaranteed for a prompt.

source: Elmoznino et al. (2025) In-Context Learning and Occam's Razor, LLM test
finding: A pretrained LLM on Mastermind did not lower prequential code length; it was worse than a naive baseline predicting the label marginal.
numbers: Prequential code length higher than a much smaller model trained on Mastermind tasks and higher than the empirical-marginal baseline (Figure 5).
limits: One LLM, one puzzle family.
agent_relevance: Do not assume a big pretrained model compresses novel rule tasks better than trivial counting. Measure with code.

source: Voita and Titov (2020) Information-Theoretic Probing with MDL (EMNLP)
finding: Measure how well model representations encode a property by total code length of labels (data plus probe), not probe accuracy. Code length separates real tasks from control tasks; accuracy often does not.
numbers: Control-task code lengths at least twice the linguistic-task ones. Layer 0: accuracy higher on control task, yet code twice as long. Variational and online codes agree; random seeds change accuracy but not MDL. Tuned selectivity probe scores 97.3 vs 97.0 for two layers.
limits: English probing tasks; pretrained encoders.
agent_relevance: Concrete case where MDL beat accuracy as a judge and resisted memorisation; same logic argues for length plus held-out in S7.

source: Chollet (2019) On the Measure of Intelligence
finding: Defines intelligence via Algorithmic Information Theory as skill-acquisition efficiency, with priors and experience controlled. Introduces ARC.
numbers: No single number; states that unlimited priors or unlimited data allow skill without generalisation.
limits: Conceptual framework.
agent_relevance: Frames why compression-minded scoring should account for prior plus experience, not only final accuracy.

source: ARC Prize 2024 Technical Report
finding: Top ARC-AGI results in 2024 came from deep-learning-guided program synthesis and test-time training, not plain prompting.
numbers: Private eval state of the art 33% to 55.5%; ARChitects 53.5% top. Semi-private/public: Berman 53.6/58.5, Akyurek 47.5/62.8, Greenblatt 43/42, o1-preview (pass@1) 18/21, Claude 3.5 Sonnet 14/21. Two humans scored 97% and 98% on private tasks.
limits: Scores count as overfit if semi-private and public differ by over 10 points absolute.
agent_relevance: Baseline context for how far scaffolds beat raw prompting on program-like tasks.

source: Liao and Gu (2025) ARC-AGI Without Pretraining (CompressARC blog)
finding: A randomly initialised network is trained per puzzle only to compress the puzzle (cross-entropy plus KL), with no pretraining; the answer comes from the compressed model. A pure MDL system.
numbers: Pass@2: 34.75% on ARC-AGI-1 training set and 20% on evaluation set; about 20 minutes per puzzle on an RTX 4070; 2000 iterations.
limits: Read through a fetch-tool summary, not raw page text. Cannot count, chain operations, detect connectivity or plan. Fragile training runs.
agent_relevance: Plain description-length minimisation alone solves about a fifth of unseen ARC tasks; also shows its limits.

source: Lake, Salakhutdinov, Tenenbaum (2015) Human-level concept learning through probabilistic program induction (Science)
finding: Bayesian program learning of handwritten characters from one example; reported to pass a visual Turing test.
numbers: Not opened this session; numbers not recorded.
limits: Known from memory only.
agent_relevance: Older computational ancestor of program-like concept learning.

source: Rissanen (1978) Modeling by shortest data description
finding: Original statement of the MDL principle.
numbers: Not opened.
limits: Memory only.
agent_relevance: Foundation for the S7 tie-break.

source: Gruenwald (2007) The Minimum Description Length Principle
finding: Standard book on MDL; stresses that codes need a good model class and are not crude program-length counts.
numbers: Not opened.
limits: Memory only.
agent_relevance: Warns against crude length counting.

source: Wikipedia: Minimum description length
finding: Says algorithmic MDL is studied within general intelligence work; reports no LLM results (per the SUBFIELDS row, opened by an earlier pass).
numbers: No numbers.
limits: Not re-opened by this agent.
agent_relevance: Starting point only.
